title: Git and CI/CD
description: Integrate Git with continuous integration and deployment pipelines to automate testing, builds, and releases.

data.text: CI/CD pipelines treat Git as the source of truth for what should be built, tested, and deployed. Advanced pipelines go beyond simple lint-and-test: they trigger selectively based on changed paths, publish artifacts, update releases, and even modify Kubernetes manifests based on branch names or tags.

CI servers listen for Git push events via webhooks. When a push arrives, the server clones the repo, checks out the commit, and runs jobs. Understanding what the CI server sees — branch names, commit messages, and environment variables — helps you design smarter triggers.

data.title: GitHub Actions workflow on push to main
data.code:
name: CI/CD

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npm test

  deploy:
    needs: build
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: ./deploy.sh "${{ github.ref_name }}"

data.text: Not every commit requires a full pipeline. Path filters let you skip expensive jobs when only documentation or scripts change. This keeps feedback fast and reduces wasted compute.

items: **Fetch depth** — Shallow clones (`fetch-depth: 1`) speed up jobs but hide history. Use full clones only when you need tags or commit ranges.
**Git tags for releases** — Tag commits in CI and push tags back to the repository so downstream consumers can pin exact versions.
**Merge queue** — Platforms like GitHub Merge Queue integrate Git merges with CI, ensuring the main branch always passes tests before merging.

data.title: CI is not a substitute for local checks
data.text: Relying entirely on CI to catch formatting or linting issues slows the feedback loop. Run fast checks locally with pre-commit hooks; use CI for checks that require the full environment.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Treat Git as the CI/CD trigger source: commits, tags, and branches drive automation.
Use path filters to avoid running expensive jobs on irrelevant changes.
Push tags and artifacts back to the repository for reproducible deployments.
Combine fast local hooks with slower server-side CI checks.
